data.title: Lysosomal cholesterol activates mTORC1 via an SLC38A9-Niemann-Pick C1 signaling complex
data.authors: Castellano BM; Thelen AM; Moldavski O; Feltes M; van der Welle REN; Mydock-McGrane L; Jiang X; van Eijkeren RJ; Davis OB; Louie SM; Perera RM; Covey DF; Nomura DK; Ory DS; Zoncu R

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human cell lines (HEK293T), CHO cells, NPC patient fibroblasts
data.finding: Establishes lysosomal cholesterol as a nutrient input that drives mTORC1 recruitment and activation at the lysosomal surface. SLC38A9 is required for cholesterol-driven mTORC1 activation through conserved cholesterol-responsive motifs, and does so independently of its arginine-sensing function; NPC1, which exports cholesterol from the lysosome, binds SLC38A9 and restrains mTORC1 through its sterol transport function. Boundary: cell lines and patient-derived fibroblasts, no organismal endpoint.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) protein kinase is a master growth regulator that becomes activated at the lysosome in response to nutrient cues. Here, we identify cholesterol, an essential building block for cellular growth, as a nutrient input that drives mTORC1 recruitment and activation at the lysosomal surface. The lysosomal transmembrane protein, SLC38A9, is required for mTORC1 activation by cholesterol through conserved cholesterol-responsive motifs. Moreover, SLC38A9 enables mTORC1 activation by cholesterol independently from its arginine-sensing function.
